problems.quote: 'tighten the repo rate' is a fixed phrase in policy discourse
problems.problem: Central banks do not 'tighten the repo rate'; they 'raise', 'hike', 'increase', or 'adjust' the repo rate. 'Tighten' collocates with 'monetary policy', 'policy stance', 'liquidity', or 'norms', not with the repo rate itself.
problems.correction: 'raise the repo rate' is a fixed phrase in policy discourse
problems.verifierReason: 'Tighten' applies to policy/stance, not the rate instrument; 'raise/hike the repo rate' is correct collocation.

problems.quote: "approve" and "acknowledge" are positive polarity verbs that become infelicitous under negation
problems.problem: Approve and acknowledge are not positive polarity items; they can be negated naturally (e.g., "did not approve" is grammatical).
problems.correction: "approve" and "acknowledge" are not positive polarity verbs; they can be negated naturally
problems.verifierReason: Approve/acknowledge are not PPIs; they negate naturally.

problems.quote: Options like "proof" or "confirmation" are positive polarity and create a semantic clash
problems.problem: Nouns like proof and confirmation are not classified as positive polarity items; polarity sensitivity applies to determiners/adverbs, not nouns.
problems.correction: Options like "proof" or "confirmation" are not polarity-sensitive nouns; they can appear in negative contexts
problems.verifierReason: Proof/confirmation are not polarity-sensitive nouns; they appear in negative contexts.

problems.quote: "Every bank did not ______ the guideline". The former means "some banks did not", the latter means "no bank did"
problems.problem: "Every bank did not follow the guideline" is ambiguous: it can mean 'not every bank followed' (some did not) or 'no bank followed'.
problems.correction: "Every bank did not ______ the guideline" is ambiguous: it can mean 'some banks did not' or 'no bank did'
problems.verifierReason: The sentence is ambiguous between 'some did not' and 'none did'.

problems.problem: Yield and benefit are verbs, not negative polarity items; the NPI licensed by 'doubts' is 'any'.
problems.correction: licensing the NPI "any" with verbs like "yield" and "benefit"
problems.verifierReason: Yield/benefit are verbs, not NPIs; the NPI is 'any'.

problems.quote: "provide" (will provide liquidity) changes the transitivity pattern and breaks the ellipsis licence
problems.problem: Both cut and provide are transitive verbs; provide does not change the transitivity pattern.
problems.correction: "provide" (will provide liquidity) maintains the transitivity pattern and fits the ellipsis licence
problems.verifierReason: Provide is transitive like cut; it maintains transitivity and ellipsis.

problems.quote: expects verbs that are mutually exclusive actions
problems.problem: The conjunction "or" does not require mutual exclusivity; it is often inclusive.
problems.correction: expects verbs that represent alternative actions
problems.verifierReason: Or does not require mutual exclusivity; 'alternative actions' is accurate.

problems.quote: exactly one follows if the premises are consistent
problems.problem: Contradictory conclusions cannot both follow, but consistent premises do not guarantee that exactly one follows; it is possible that neither follows.
problems.correction: at most one follows; neither may follow
problems.verifierReason: Original claims exactly one conclusion follows from consistent premises; but contradictory conclusions may have neither follow. Correction states at most one follows, neither may follow. Accurate.

problems.quote: which is the obverse of “All managers are engineers”
problems.problem: “No non‑engineers are managers” is the converse of the obverse (or obverted converse), not the obverse itself. The obverse of “All managers are engineers” is “No managers are non‑engineers”.
problems.correction: which is the converse of the obverse of “All managers are engineers”
problems.verifierReason: "No non-engineers are managers" is converse of obverse, not obverse. Correction correctly identifies it as converse of obverse.

problems.quote: is the contrapositive of “Some teachers are not students”
problems.problem: The contrapositive of “Some teachers are not students” (O) is “Some non‑students are not non‑teachers”, not “Some non‑students are not teachers”.
problems.correction: is not the contrapositive of “Some teachers are not students”
problems.verifierReason: Contrapositive of O proposition "Some teachers are not students" is "Some non-students are not non-teachers". Original misidentifies; correction denies false claim.

problems.quote: it is distributed in (1) (subject of A)
problems.problem: In premise (1) “All A are B”, the middle term B is the predicate of an A proposition and is undistributed; the subject A is distributed.
problems.correction: it is undistributed in (1) (predicate of A)
problems.verifierReason: In "All A are B", middle term B is predicate of A, undistributed. Original says distributed as subject; correction says undistributed as predicate. Correct.

problems.quote: “manage to avoid” implies the crisis never materialised, clashing with the presupposed existence of the crisis
problems.problem: “Manage” presupposes difficulty of the action, not existence of the complement event; “avoid” entails the crisis did not occur, so there is no presupposed existence to clash with.
problems.correction: “manage to avoid” presupposes difficulty of avoidance, not crisis existence; “avoid” entails non-occurrence, so no existence presupposition to clash
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates presupposition; correction accurately describes 'manage' and 'avoid'.

problems.problem: Simple past “reported” is a tense form, not an aspect; “perfective” is an aspectual category, not the standard name for the simple past in English grammar.
problems.correction: simple past (reported) presents it as complete
problems.verifierReason: 'Perfective' is aspect, not tense; correction uses 'simple past'.

problems.problem: A governor is a type of member (hyponymy), not a part of a member (meronymy); the part–whole chain is misanalysed.
problems.correction: meronymy (part-of: committee → member); hyponymy (type-of: member → governor)
problems.verifierReason: Governor is a type of member, not part; correction splits relations correctly.

problems.correction: tighten, hike, raise, increase (synonyms/co-hyponyms in policy tightening domain)
problems.verifierReason: Terms are synonyms/co-hyponyms, not hyponyms of increase; correction reflects that.
